title: Split Array Largest Sum
approach: Binary search on maximum segment sum
statement: Split a nonnegative array into exactly k nonempty contiguous subarrays while minimizing the largest subarray sum.
explanation: Binary-search the maximum allowed sum; greedily count how many segments are needed under that bound.

title: Fizz Buzz
statement: Return the strings from 1 through n, replacing multiples of three with Fizz, five with Buzz, and both with FizzBuzz.
explanation: Check divisibility by 15 first, then 3 and 5, otherwise emit the number.

title: Arithmetic Slices
statement: Count contiguous subarrays of length at least three whose adjacent differences are all equal.
explanation: When the current difference matches the previous one, extend all arithmetic slices ending at the previous index and add one new slice.

title: Third Maximum Number
statement: Return the third distinct maximum value, or the maximum if fewer than three distinct values exist.
explanation: Maintain the three largest distinct values while scanning the array.

title: Add Strings
statement: Add two nonnegative integers represented as decimal strings without converting the full strings to integers.
explanation: Add digits from right to left with a carry and append the resulting digits in reverse order.

title: Partition Equal Subset Sum
statement: Determine whether an integer array can be partitioned into two subsets with equal sums.
explanation: If the total is even, use descending 0/1 knapsack DP to determine whether a subset sums to half the total.

title: Pacific Atlantic Water Flow
statement: Return cells from which water can flow to both the Pacific and Atlantic oceans, flowing only to equal or lower neighboring heights.
explanation: Search inward from each ocean border in reverse, moving to neighbors at least as high as the current cell.
example: heights=[[1,2,2],[3,2,3],[2,4,5]] -> cells reachable from both borders

title: Battleships in a Board
statement: Count battleships on a board where ships are straight horizontal or vertical runs of X cells and ships do not touch.
explanation: Count an X only when there is no X immediately above or to its left.

title: Maximum XOR of Two Numbers in an Array
statement: Find the maximum XOR of any two values in an integer array.
explanation: Build the answer from the highest bit down, testing whether two prefixes can produce each candidate bit.

title: Reconstruct Original Digits from English
statement: Given shuffled letters spelling English digit names concatenated together, reconstruct the original digits in ascending order.
explanation: Use letters unique to selected number words to count those digits first, then derive overlapping digit counts in dependency order.
